clock_fraction_30: Slovak toward-hour HALF: "pol deviatej" == half of the ninth == 08:30
(bare_half_to + toward_hour_12h).  As in Czech, the half names the coming
hour with a genitive-feminine ordinal agreeing with elided "hodiny", and
takes no connector.  Citation: Slovník súčasného slovenského jazyka (JULS
SAV, slovnik.juls.savba.sk), s.v. "pol": "pol siedmej" glossed as 6.30 h.
clock_fraction_45: Slovak THREE QUARTERS toward the coming hour: "trištvrte na deväť" == 08:45

marker_last: Slovak "last/previous" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm (vzor "pekný").
The locative "v minulom týždni" and the genitive "minulého roka" are the
ordinary spoken forms.  Jazykovedný ústav Ľ. Štúra SAV, Slovníkový portál --
Morfológia slovenského jazyka, skloňovanie prídavných mien.
marker_na: Slovak toward-hour connector "na" ("onto"): the fraction names how far the
clock has advanced INTO the hour that is coming, so the hour spoken after
"na" is the NEXT one -- "štvrť na deväť" == a quarter onto the ninth ==
08:15, "trištvrte na deväť" == three quarters onto the ninth == 08:45.
The same construction is spelled with "na" in Belarusian and Ukrainian
Citation: Slovník súčasného slovenského jazyka (Jazykovedný ústav Ľ. Štúra
SAV, slovnik.juls.savba.sk), s.v. "štvrť": "štvrť na osem" glossed as
7.15 h -- a worked numeric example naming the COMING hour.
marker_next: Slovak "next/following" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm.  "budúci"
is the soft (vzor "cudzí") stem, "nasledujúci" likewise.  Jazykovedný ústav
Ľ. Štúra SAV, Morfológia slovenského jazyka.

scope_unit_century: Slovak "century".  After the "v"/"vo" preposition the noun stands in the
locative -- "v 20. storočí" -- so listing the nominative alone left the noun
stranded and the ordinal was read as a clock hour instead.  The locative is
spelled like the genitive plural ("päť storočí" = five centuries), so the
order that binds it requires the written ordinal dot -- the only thing that
tells "v 20. storočí" from "v 20 storočí", twenty centuries.
